# Craft Skill @ Stage 11 — Abstract Emerge

> developed 2026-07-24.

## Crosswalk (from unified ladder)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IST Stage# | 11 |
| Canonical name | Abstract Emerge |
| Altitude | `orange` (Worldcentric emerging) |
| MHC Order | 10 (Abstract) |
| Kegan | 3→4 |
| Identity band | Worldcentric emerging |

## Expression on this line

Craft skill at Order 10 is craft mastery: expert-level skill that operates beyond conscious
rule-following, producing innovative work that transcends inherited tradition. The master
craftsperson who can improvise within the tradition, innovate beyond it, and teach others
to do the same — this is the craft equivalent of the artist who has so thoroughly internalized
the rules that they can break them productively.

The key advance over Stage 10 is that craft skill is now *abstract* — it can be reasoned about
as a general phenomenon (what makes expertise possible? what enables creative innovation?)
rather than just practiced in specific contexts.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** the felt fluency of expert craft — the master craftsperson who works beyond conscious
  rule-following.
- **UR:** the capacity to innovate within and beyond inherited tradition, producing genuinely
  new craft expressions.
- **LL:** a craft culture that values mastery and innovation — communities that support expert
  development and creative risk-taking.
- **LR:** the institutional structures (master-apprentice systems, craft awards, innovation
  programs) that recognize and support craft mastery.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** mastery as ego — the master craftsperson who becomes identified with
  their expertise, unable to learn from others.
- **Dark allergy:** mastery absence — the individual who cannot or will not develop expert-level
  craft skill.
- **Golden addiction:** claiming to have achieved formal craft modeling (Stage 12) while
  actually just demonstrating expert-level craft without formal analysis.
- **Golden allergy:** refusing to engage with craft mastery because it seems "elitist,"
  clinging to amateur or intermediate craft practice.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Expert-level skill:** the craftsperson demonstrates mastery that operates beyond conscious
  rule-following.
- **Creative innovation:** the craftsperson produces genuinely new work that transcends
  inherited tradition.
- **Teaching capacity:** the master can transmit their expertise to others through mentorship
  and demonstration.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:** Dreyfus & Dreyfus, *Mind over Machine* (expert skill as post-rule-following);
Csikszentmihalyi, *Creativity* (creative mastery as flow); Polanyi, *The Tacit Dimension*
(expert knowledge as tacit).
**Open joints:** How does craft mastery shade into formal craft modeling (Stage 12)?
**Research debt:** pairs with `10-concrete-peak` (complex craft integration) and
`12-formal-landmark` (formal craft modeling).
